Ibn Umar explained four habits others noticed, touching only the Yemeni corners, wearing tanned shoes, dyeing with henna and delaying ihram, as following what he saw the Prophet do.
Whatever is innovated that is not in harmony with the principles of the religion is rejected.
Abdullah said the best talk is Allah's Book and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad.
The Prophet censured people who avoided something he did and allowed, saying he knew Allah better than they and feared Him more.
Umar urged holding to the Book that guided the Prophet, who prayed for Ibn Abbas to be taught it, and Ibn Umar pledged obedience by Allah's Laws and Sunnah.
Umar said the Prophet and Abu Bakr must be followed, Quran and Sunna strengthen honesty, the best speech is Allah's Book, the best way Muhammad's, and heresies the worst.
People followed the Prophet in wearing and discarding gold rings, he forbade continuous fasting, Ali's scroll cursed innovators in Medina, and the Prophet rebuked those avoiding what he himself did.
